activation_checkpointing.What is activation checkpointing, and wh: Store only some activations and recompute the others during backward. It trades extra compute for less memory.
activation_checkpointing.Which activations dominate memory in tra: Per-layer attention and MLP intermediates, which scale with batch times sequence times hidden size (and heads times sequence squared without FlashAttention).
activation_checkpointing.How does torch.utils.checkpoint recomput: The forward runs without saving intermediates. In backward, the segment's forward is rerun from its saved inputs to rebuild the graph, then backpropagated.
activation_checkpointing.What goes wrong with randomness such as: Dropout masks would differ in the recomputation, giving wrong gradients. PyTorch saves and restores the RNG state for the recompute.
activation_checkpointing.How do you choose which layers or segmen: Checkpoint the layers with the most memory per unit of recompute, often each transformer block, or sqrt(N) segments.
activation_checkpointing.Roughly how much extra compute does full: About one extra forward pass (about 33% more compute). Selective checkpointing recomputes only cheap but large ops such as attention softmax.
activation_checkpointing.Checkpointing versus offloading activati: Offloading avoids recompute but needs PCIe bandwidth to overlap. It is good when compute is the bottleneck and the transfer can be hidden.

packed_sequence_mask.What is sequence packing, and why does i: Concatenate several short documents into one fixed-length row instead of padding each one. There is less wasted compute.
packed_sequence_mask.What goes wrong if you pack documents bu: Tokens attend across document boundaries and positions continue across documents, so the model learns false context.
packed_sequence_mask.Build the block-diagonal causal mask fro: Allowed when both tokens are in the same document and j <= i. Padding rows must attend to at least one position, such as themselves, to avoid NaN.
packed_sequence_mask.What is cu_seqlens, and how do FlashAtte: Cumulative document boundaries [0, l1, l1+l2, ...]. Varlen kernels use them to run attention per segment with no dense mask.
packed_sequence_mask.With RoPE, why must position ids restart: Each document should see positions starting at 0, as in training without packing. Otherwise RoPE encodes offsets that are wrong.
packed_sequence_mask.Packing changes how many tokens each doc: Per-token averaging treats packed and unpacked data the same. Per-sequence averaging must count documents, not rows.
packed_sequence_mask.Greedy bin packing versus sorting by len: Greedy packing minimizes padding but mixes lengths, and sorting creates length-biased batches. Truncation discards data.

chunked_cross_entropy.Why can the LM-head logits be the larges: It is tokens times vocab: 16k * 128k * 4 bytes is about 8 GB in fp32 (plus the same again for the gradient).
chunked_cross_entropy.What does chunking the cross-entropy sav: Only one chunk of logits exists at a time. But autograd saves each chunk's logits or probabilities for backward, so the total is the same.
chunked_cross_entropy.Walk through which tensors autograd save: Without checkpointing, every chunk's softmax output is saved. With it, only the hidden states are saved and the logits are recomputed per chunk.
chunked_cross_entropy.How do you keep the mean correct when ch: Sum the per-chunk losses and divide by the total number of non-ignored tokens, not by the chunk count.
chunked_cross_entropy.Write the gradient of cross-entropy with: softmax - onehot. A fused kernel computes the gradient for a chunk right away and writes grad_hidden and grad_W, never storing the logits.
chunked_cross_entropy.Chunk-and-recompute versus a fused linea: Chunking is simple but recomputes, and a fused kernel is fastest but custom. Vocabulary parallelism shards the vocabulary across GPUs and needs communication.
chunked_cross_entropy.How do you choose the chunk size, and wh: Balance the peak memory of one chunk against per-chunk overhead. Tiny chunks mean kernel-launch overhead; one chunk means no savings.

lora.What is LoRA, and why does low-rank adap: Freeze W and learn a low-rank update B A. Fine-tuning updates have low intrinsic rank, so few parameters capture them.
lora.What are A and B, and which one is initi: A (r x in) is random, B (out x r) is zero, so B A = 0 at the start and the model begins exactly as the base.
lora.What does alpha over rank scaling do?: It scales the update by alpha / r, so changing r does not require retuning the learning rate much.
lora.How do you freeze the base weight and tr: requires_grad False on the base weights, and only pass the adapter parameters to the optimizer.
lora.How do you merge LoRA weights for infere: W' = W + (alpha / r) B A. Merged once, there is no extra latency.
lora.LoRA versus full fine-tuning: where does: Large domain shifts or new capabilities. Low rank can underfit, and it learns less but also forgets less.
lora.How do you choose rank and which layers: Start small (8 to 16) and apply it to all linear layers, including the MLP. Increase the rank if the task is hard.

qlora.What is QLoRA, and how does it combine q: Keep the base weights quantized to 4 bits and train LoRA adapters in higher precision on top.
qlora.Why can the base model stay quantized du: The base is frozen: it only needs a forward and backward through its values, never an update.
qlora.How do you dequantize the base weight in: Compute w approximately as q * scale (per row or block) on the fly into bf16, then run the matmul.
qlora.Which tensors receive gradients?: Only the LoRA A and B matrices. Gradients flow through the dequantized base to the input but the base weights get none.
qlora.How is the per-row scale computed?: The max absolute value of the row divided by the largest quantized level.
qlora.What precision does real QLoRA use, such: NF4 levels match normally distributed weights, and double quantization also compresses the scales. Paged optimizers handle memory spikes.
qlora.What quality do you lose compared with L: Usually close to LoRA on a bf16 base, with a small loss from quantization error, bigger at very low bits.

paged_attention.What is PagedAttention, and what problem: It manages the KV cache in fixed-size blocks like OS virtual memory, removing fragmentation and over-reservation.
paged_attention.How does a block table work?: Each sequence has a list mapping its logical block index to a physical block id in a shared pool.
paged_attention.How do you map a logical token position: page = pos // block_size; offset = pos % block_size; physical = block_table[page].
paged_attention.How do you gather keys and values for at: Look up each position's physical block and offset, gather from the pools into contiguous K and V (or have the kernel read directly), then attend.
paged_attention.What happens with the last partially fil: Only the first (length mod block_size) slots are valid. Mask or slice the rest.
paged_attention.What does paging enable, such as prefix: Several sequences can point to the same prefix blocks, and copy on write handles divergence. This enables beam search and parallel sampling cheaply.
paged_attention.What does the extra indirection cost?: Extra lookups and non-contiguous memory reads, plus kernel complexity. Block size trades waste against lookup overhead.
